children: The following are significant news stories, press reports and events on Monday. ALL TIMES GMT (Poland: GMT + 2 hours):

A Polish court sought to have Russian spy Pavel Rubtsov pursued worldwide for espionage against Poland, but the police refused to submit the request to Interpol, arguing that it would be inconsistent with the organisation’s constitution, Rzeczpospolita daily reported.

There is no real threat of any practical disruption to the work of the Monetary Policy Council (MPC) from the motion in parliament to bring Governor Adam Glapinski before a State Tribunal, MPC member Joanna Tyrowicz told Rzeczpospolita.

Polish nationalist opposition party Law and Justice (PiS) hopes it can build influence over private broadcaster TVN, Newsweek reported. TVN is owned by Warner Bros Discovery (WBD.O) which has been acquired by Paramount Skydance in its blockbuster $110 billion takeover.

Changes to the Polish tax system balance eachother out, because the 'Santa Claus' era of tax policy is over, Deputy Finance Minister Jaroslaw Neneman told Puls Biznesu daily. He said the government was looking for tax reforms that would be acceptable for society, like changes to flat-rate income tax and introducing a new corporate income tax rate.

The Constitutional Tribunal is set to rule on whether the Bank Guarantee Fund (BFG) can recover billions of zlotys from the assets of the insolvent Getin Noble Bank ahead of other creditors, Dziennik Gazeta Prawna reported. For those with Swiss franc-denominated loans who won court cases with the bank, this represents a chance to recover a portion of their money, according to the newspaper.
Popular European, Japanese, and Korean brands are offering discounts in response to pressure from Chinese competitors, Rzeczpospolita reported.

Poland has received informal approval to join the GCAP - a joint project between Japan, the UK, and Italy to develop a new combat aircraft - as an observer, Rzeczpospolita reported. The next step is to submit a formal application, but a final decision has yet to be made by the government, according to the newspaper.
